subject: TiltBridge — pricing & packaging clarifications
messages:
From: Sam Tillman <sam.tillman@tiltbridge.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: TiltBridge Procurement <procurement@tiltbridge.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: TiltBridge pricing & packaging questions

Hi Rachel —

Thanks again for last week's demo. Procurement ran the initial bill-of-materials against our budget and surfaced a few areas where we need clarification before we take this to budget committee: 

1) Discount stacking: does Redwood allow a combination of committed-usage discount + multi-year credit? If so, how do they stack for our expected 18M tokens/month baseline?

2) Escape hatch mechanics: if we commit to a 12-month reserved capacity plan, what does an early reduction look like? We need an example of how credits/charges are applied if throughput drops 30% in Q4.

3) Packaging: we are evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated for the pilot. Can you provide side-by-side unit economics for the pilot (100k monthly tokens) and projected steady-state (18M tokens/month)?

4) Competitive parity: one of our teams flagged an incumbent offering (EdgeStream) that claims lower per-token pricing at scale. Can you point us to the direct comparables and any migration credits you would apply?

Attaching a short RFP worksheet with the questions filled in (TiltBridge_RFP_questions.xlsx). Would love a short written response we can share with procurement, and a timing estimate if you can put together a formal quote.

Best,
Sam
Sam Tillman
Head of Platform & Integrations | TiltBridge
procurement@tiltbridge.com


From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>

Cc: TiltBridge Procurement <procurement@tiltbridge.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TiltBridge pricing & packaging questions

Hi Sam —

Appreciate the clear list — that helped a lot. High-level answers below, and I attached a short pricing sheet and an excerpt of the SOW so procurement can scan the operational terms. I can pull a formal quote by EOD tomorrow once you confirm whether you want Hosted pilot or Dedicated pilot.

Quick answers:
- Discount stacking: we support committed usage discounts (volume tiers) + a separate long-term prepay credit. They stack additively on the per-token base rate — e.g., a 15% committed tier + 10% prepay credit results in ~23.5% effective reduction (we apply sequentially per our billing calculator). Details in TiltBridge_Pricing_Sheet_v2.pdf.
- Escape hatch (reserved capacity): standard language is a 60-day notice with pro-rated exit credits. For a 30% reduction mid-term we typically apply a one-time reconciliation based on committed units vs consumed; if prepay was used we issue remaining credit as account balance (not cash). Example table included in the pricing sheet.
- Hosted vs Dedicated (pilot economics): Hosted has lower upfront and better burst handling; Dedicated gives predictable latency and usually lower long-run unit cost at very high sustained throughput. I put two scenarios in the attached PDF (pilot 100k tokens / steady-state 18M tokens).
- Competitive parity / migration credits: we evaluate migration credits case-by-case. For competitors with contractual exit costs, we commonly offer an onboarding credit up to 3 months of committed spend to offset penalties; details tied to contract term and committed spend.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm pilot mode (Hosted or Dedicated) — I can tailor the formal quote.
2) 30-min procurement + engineering sync tomorrow at 10:00 PT?
3) If procurement prefers, we can include a draft escape-hatch clause for legal review in the quote.

Attachments: TiltBridge_Pricing_Sheet_v2.pdf, Redwood_SOW_excerpt.docx

Thanks — looking forward to narrowing this down.

Rachel Kim
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2026 10:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: TiltBridge pricing options (notes)

Rachel / Marcus — quick internal note before we send the formal quote. Copying some bullets for the procurement call: 

- Suggested commercial: 12-month reserved (committed tokens) + 6% prepay credit for 12-mo prepay or 10% credit for 24-mo prepay.
- Escape hatch option: 60-day notice + phased reconciliation. If reduction >20% we apply a tiered credit: 30% reduction -> 50% of remaining prepay returned as account credit, 30% retained to cover provisioning costs. (We can soften for strategic customers.)
- Migration concession: offer a one-time onboarding credit equal to 8 weeks of committed spend for customers with documented egress/termination penalties from incumbent.
- Pilot fit: recommend Hosted pilot (less friction) but bake a dedicated migration discount if they convert within 90 days.

I also pushed the HubSpot deal record with these terms: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/3257/TLT-2026-0012 (internal notes updated).

Jordan Blake
Director, Commercial Strategy

2) Can you prepare a short draft amendment with the escape-hatch language for our counsel? They want the exact 60-day notice text and the math for any credits.

If you can get those two items into a DocuSign-ready package (quote + amendment) by tomorrow EOD we can push this through procurement and aim to return a PO next week. I've looped procurement on this reply.
